children: The Mexican peso depreciated more than its major international peers on Thursday after minutes from the Bank of Mexico's latest monetary policy meeting showed three of five governing board members said future interest-rate cuts could be considered if the inflation outlook improves.
was last trading at 18.19 per dollar, down around 1.2% at 1851 GMT, and while it had already been losing ground earlier in the day, it fell even more following the document's release.
Bank of Mexico's minutes heightened concerns that the yield spread with the United States would continue to narrow in the event of further rate cuts
Mexico's headline consumer price index accelerated in September, though less than expected, while core inflation continued to moderate but remained at the upper end of the target range

The peso is under pressure since the central bank held its interest rate at 6.50% in September and decoupled from Fed policy, fueling fears that a narrowing yield gap will reduce the appeal of "carry trade" operations
Today's movement indicate that international investors are beginning to lose interest in Mexican assets, said Jacobo Rodríguez, an analyst at the firm Roga Capital

He noted that 18.50 pesos per dollar represents a significant technical resistance level, which could be reached in the short term if nervousness persists, also driven by tensions in the Middle East and the U.S. midterm elections in November
